claim: T55h: the all-pairs kNN flow ceiling on this machine should be ~2*10^4 neurons (the n^2*8 B transient distance matrix plus kNN sort temporaries exhaust RAM), NOT the naive 50-60k estimate that only counts the D array - so flow beyond ~2*10^4 requires O(1)-per-neuron spatial search, not all-pairs.
verdict: SUPPORTED (measured on this box, dim=2, k=8, mu0=0.12, A=120): ms/step scales as n^1.76 (t = 2.96e-7 * n^1.76) up to n=5000 then the exponent rises to ~2.06 from 5000->20000 once the D array stops fitting in cache - flow is effectively n^2 at the ceiling; measured values n=1000 66.3, n=5000 1230.2, n=20000 25422.5 ms/step. RAM is the binding wall: the kNN sort temporaries blow past the n^2*8 B estimate (peak WS 22.6 GB at n=20000 while the D array is only 3.2 GB) - the measured ceiling on this 31.7 GB box is ~2*10^4, not the naive 50-60k. n=40000 would peak ~90 GB (not run: would risk a hard OOM). Conclusion: scaling beyond ~2*10^4 needs O(1)-per-neuron spatial search (T67), not all-pairs.
